newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto Sun buyers say no FinPost bid.
newsitem.headline: Toronto Sun buyers say no FinPost bid.

text.p: The management group poised to complete its buyout on Tuesday of Toronto Sun Publishing Corp wants to keep the company's stake in the Financial Post, Toronto Sun chief financial officer Bruce Jackson said.
Despite news reports to the contrary, the management group said it has not received an offer from Conrad Black-controlled Southam Inc for the 60.2 percent it holds of the national business tabloid.
"We don't have any offer for the Financial Post," Jackson told Reuters in telephone interview.
"Southam was in the (Toronto Sun) data room back in June or July...I believe they made an offer at that time for the Financial Post. And I think obviously there is interest there," Jackson added.

The Canadian Press newsagency reported late Thursday that Southam had made an offer for the Financial Post as the final days ticked away ahead of Tuesday's vote by shareholders on the management group's C$16 per share bid for Toronto Sun.
But the Financial Post carried a report on Friday which said Southam had not made an offer since July.
Conrad Black's Hollinger Inc, which controls Southam, owns about 20 percent of the Financial Post.
CP quoted David Radler, Southam's associate chief executive of and president of Hollinger, as saying he did not know if Southam's offer for the Post would succeed.
"It's in the hands of (Toronto Sun president Paul) Godfrey," CP quoted Radler as saying.
